title: Composition of Counter-Program Runs
statement: Let $R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, let $P$ be a counter program over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, and fix an input bit string $x$. For every abstract state $s$ and $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$, running for $a+b$ steps from $s$ gives the same state as running for $a$ steps and then for $b$ further steps.
hypotheses_covered: $R\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\Lambda$ is a set of labels.
$P$ is a counter program over $R$ registers and labels in $\Lambda$.
An input bit string $x$ is fixed.
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, $x$ an input bit
string and $s$ an abstract state. For all $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$, running $a + b$ steps from $s$
is the same as running $a$ steps and then $b$ further steps:
$\mathrm{run}_{P,x}(s, a + b) = \mathrm{run}_{P,x}(\mathrm{run}_{P,x}(s, a), b)$.
